title: Session-aware micro-batching to reduce jitter for streaming chat completions
creator: Asha Patel
description: Streaming chat workloads show high latency jitter and occasional tail spikes when short interactive sessions are co-batched with long, multi-turn sessions. The runtime's continuous batching mixes heterogeneous sequences which increases KV cache pressure and leads to uneven GPU memory fragmentation. This ticket proposes a session-aware batch formation heuristic plus KV tiering and memory-slab reservations to minimize tail jitter while preserving throughput and cost efficiency.
acceptance_criteria: p50 latency for streaming chat <= baseline+5ms
p95 latency reduced by >= 20% for mixed short+long session traces
jitter (stddev of per-token latency) reduced by >= 25% for test traces
GPU memory high-water events reduced by >= 50% under mixed workload replay
no regression in token-generation correctness or stream order; existing tests pass
feature behind runtime feature flag; rollout steps validated in canary
proposal: Implement a session-aware micro-batcher extension to the continuous batcher: tag streaming requests with 'session_length_hint' and 'interactive_priority'. The batcher will form micro-batches preferentially grouping requests with similar remaining-token distributions and session affinity (same session ID or same client). Introduce two KV cache tiers (hot and warm): hot KV remains pinned in GPU memory for active interactive sessions while warm KV is kept compressed in DRAM with fast restore paths. Add GPU slab reservations for hot-KV allocations to avoid fragmentation by large batched KV swaps.
design_notes: Batching rules: prefer same-session coalescing, max_microbatch_size=8, max_latency_budget_ms=12 for streaming tokens
Session hints: router supplies 'estimated_remaining_tokens' calculated from client-side heuristics + historical averages
KV tiers: hot (GPU resident), warm (host DRAM with compressed/KV snapshot), cold (evicted to disk)
Memory: implement per-GPU slab allocator with separate pools for model activations, KV hot slabs, and transient batch buffers
Fallback: when hot slab exhausted, soft-evict least-recently-used session KV to warm tier with async restore
implementation_plan: 1) Add session metadata plumbing: accept 'session_hint' in streaming API and propagate through router and runtime
2) Extend batcher: implement microbatch builder that groups by (session_bucket, estimated_remaining_tokens_bucket)
3) KV tiering prototype: implement in-memory warm cache and GPU pin/unpin API
4) GPU slab allocator: add pool accounting and reservation APIs in runtime memory manager
5) Integration tests: replay production traces in perf cluster; verify no correctness regression
6) Shadow deployment: enable behind feature flag for 5% traffic; collect metrics for 2 weeks
7) Gradual rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> full after metrics validation
rollout_plan: Canary: enable in runtime-rc on staging and shadow 100% production traffic to collect metrics
Enable for 5% live traffic with automatic rollback if p95 latency increases or GPU OOMs detected
Monitoring: dashboard alerts for p95 > baseline*1.15, GPU OOMs count > 1 per hour, KV restore latency > 100ms
Feature flag controls: microbatching on/off, hot-KV size cap, slab-reserve-percentage
Post-rollout: run 48-hour regression job that replays typical PLG and enterprise workloads
risks: Increased complexity in batcher may introduce bugs affecting stream ordering or partial flush behavior
KV tiering introduces restore latency spikes if restore path isn't sufficiently optimized
Memory reservations could reduce peak throughput if reserved too aggressively
Client-side session hints may be inaccurate and lead to suboptimal grouping
Edge-case interactions with existing autoscaler and Dedicated capacity policies
comments: 2026-02-11 Asha Patel: Initial triage — observed p95 spikes during mixed short/long session replay. Proposed session-aware grouping. Assigned to Miguel.

2026-02-17 Miguel Torres: Spike reprobed in perf-cluster; confirmed KV growth during mixed traces. Implemented microbatch builder prototype locally. Observed 18% p95 improvement in synthetic trace when grouping by remaining_tokens bucket.
2026-02-23 Riley Chen (code-review): Design looks good. Questions: how will this interact with existing latency SLO-driven failure policies? Recommend adding hard-timeout flush to prevent starvation.

2026-02-26 Miguel Torres: Added hard-timeout flush to microbatcher (12ms). Implemented hot/warm KV prototype with compressed DRAM snapshot. Warm->hot restore currently ~42ms median; optimizing deserialization next.

2026-03-01 Priya Nair (perf): Shadow runs on 5% traffic for 48h show p95 improved 23% and jitter down 28%. Two warm-restore spikes at 210ms correlated with DRAM GC on a host — mitigation: pin warm caches to non-GC memory region.
2026-03-02 Miguel Torres: Preparing canary rollout PR and dashboard. Adding alerts for kv_restore_latency_ms > 150ms and gpu_oom_count > 0. Follow-up ticket planned for warm-cache GC-proofing.
